You open a comm channel and faintly hear soldiers reporting to a superior. When the image resolves, the woman before you is wearing a general's insignia.

"The truth," General $personName explains to your visible surprise, "is that the previous target was eliminated for reasons unknown. Our current difficulty is an armament procurement project, a rather large order. By any means available to you, deliver three mothballed Yoshura-class capital ships to me. Are you interested?"

You consider the unusual commission carefully...

text:
"Excellent work." The aging general claps a hand on your shoulder.

"See that battlecruiser? The old thing is scheduled to be transferred to Enigma III Industrial Station for dismantling in half a month. Would you care to take a look?"

You step onto a broad side deck. Dense turret clusters sit in rectangular groups near the centerline. This appears to be a Yoshura variant, though its distinctive paint scheme makes clear you have never seen a similar ship in port.

On the command room's long table sits a palm-sized holoprojector. The surrounding compartment is dark and powerless, yet the device continues to display the bust of a man.

"Less a vessel of glory than a crystallized memory."

The general mutters the words while walking ahead, then turns sharply. The cybernetic eye on her right side locks onto you.

"Your completed task was only a test. Before we reach the real matter, let us talk about something else."

---- You follow the general through a long, dim maintenance conduit and out through starboard airlock A ----

The noon glare forces you to narrow your eyes. Her voice cuts through it: "All Enigma witnessed our love. Neither of us was ready for separation, but the gender revolution had reached its turning point." Her voice catches. "He always..."

"It was an external campaign, a large-scale struggle against the Hegemony. In the original plan, alongside full internal mobilization, the vultures of war were already circling. Two fleets crawled like beasts along the asteroid-strewn edge of the system for days, carefully turning their most aggressive formations toward each other. Fleet maneuvers on that scale were a spectacle even in this Sector. Detachments and scout wings stretched as far as three light-years.

"The first day went well. Battles ignited across four fronts, and the Hegemony vanguard took severe losses; one aviation battleship was nearly reduced to scrap.

"The second day began with a military mutiny. He led the defectors in an axial jump, seized a prototype Yoshura variant, and tore open the campaign from within."
options: 0:vft_continue:You cannot help leaning forward, eager to hear the rest.

text:
"After the battle, the traitors made no further move. They simply left the system. But the Valkyrians never stopped looking for them." The general pauses, her expression unreadable.

"In truth, a report of possible fleet signatures in close orbit around a certain system stayed on my personal terminal until I retired from the front line. That is where he is hiding. If command learns of it, treason and a gallows await him.

"This must end, but I do not want him to die in humiliation. That is why I found you. You are the only captain I believe has both patience and strength enough to handle him quietly. When it is done, you may keep every prize."

text:
After a longer conversation, you learn that he was once the refit chief of the general's flagship, obsessed with modification to an almost unimaginable degree.

"What... do you think?" the general asks, her voice trembling and distant.

0:vft_type_love:"Isn't this honored flagship covered in proof of his love for you?"
1:vft_type_hate:"Hatred cuts as deeply as love."
2:vft_type_normal:"A fatal kind of foolishness, wasn't it?"

text:
To your surprise, you receive his comm request first. When you accept, he begins speaking as if he already knows why you came.

"You are the one she sent, aren't you? This day did not arrive as late as I expected."

The wanderer leader's eyelids droop. He looks less like a fleet commander than a man weathered by too many ports and too much empty space.

"Years in the void cost us dearly. This ship was once full of revolutionary hope. We tried to build our own utopia, but on the new world we ran out of fuel money. Alliance merchants manipulated a fragile colonial economy, made famine, and squeezed every credit from the people."

"When I realized destroying trade fleets only made our own survival impossible, I understood what exile truly meant."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"You once loved each other. How did it come to this?"

text: "At some point, communication stopped. Both sides silently insisted on their own justice through action. On the eve of the great battle, my followers and I hid old carbines and electromagnetic rifles inside supply crates and moved them aboard. We could not let the chance pass. The crushing weight of interstellar power was suffocating the movement. We had to reach the edge of Valkyrian force projection. It was our only road out."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"I cannot deny that it was a great struggle."

text:
"We seized a detachment with the speed of thunder. Before anyone exposed us, revolutionaries boarded a prototype Yoshura variant and killed the defending foot-lancers. Their pulse deflection fields failed completely under concentrated fire. The fall of that battleship became the movement's greatest achievement.

"The outpost was our final target. Once armed mobs stripped it bare, we broke from the organization and became residents of the silent void. From the captured battleship's frame and the outpost's secrets, I built this war machine. I chose to defend the meaning of my life with iron and blood until the final moment."

Resolve hardens in his eyes as he raises a hand to cut the channel.
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"Allow me one last question. What do you think of her now?"

text:
"She is the only one, in every moment."

Both sides fall silent. After a while, he looks at you, and the stars in his eyes seem never to have gone out. He cuts the connection with final resolve. His transmission ends, announcing both the end of a story and the beginning of a battle.

"I hate her."

The channel falls silent. The flagship shudders violently, and from beyond the bridge you hear someone shouting, "Incoming fire! Incoming fire!"

"From the moment we abandoned the organization, there was nothing left between us."

Static rolls through the channel, and the connection dies.
